clue.text: Member going on about rise

indicators.note: one piece going on after another means it follows it in the answer

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about
a limb is a member of the body, an arm or a leg

explanation.surface: A club member keeps going on about a promotion.
explanation.definitionFit: To rise is to go upward, the same as to ascend a slope.

clue.text: After church a large number, unexpectedly freed, sloped off

indicators.note: after church means the following pieces come after the church abbreviation

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

indicators.note: unexpectedly indicates the letters of freed turn up in a surprising order

explanation.surface: After church a crowd of people, suddenly released, slipped away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sloped off' looks like 'left quietly' but means bevelled; FERED is the rearrangement of FREED.
explanation.definitionFit: A chamfered edge has been cut away at an angle, bevelled.

clue.text: Thought Latin best

parts.note: an idea is a thought

explanation.surface: Thinking that a Latin education was the finest.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideal means perfect, the most excellent imaginable.

clue.text: Playful repartee only adolescents find tolerable?

definitions.text: Playful repartee only adolescents find tolerable?

parts.words: Playful repartee only adolescents find tolerable?
parts.note: the second half jokingly reads the word as ..., something only bearable at a certain age

explanation.walkthrough: The opening words define it; the rest whimsically splits the word into BAD IN AGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Badinage is light teasing banter.

clue.text: Setting off without cash is very surprising

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the setting-off word goes around the cash

parts.note: setting off on a journey is starting
L stands for pounds, British cash

explanation.surface: Setting out on a trip with no money is an astonishing thing to do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but means 'outside' here: L, the pound sign, goes inside STARTING.
explanation.definitionFit: Something astonishing or alarming makes you jump, the sense of startle.

clue.text: Staunch support

explanation.surface: A loyal supporter.
explanation.definitionFit: To halt the flow of blood, and a plant's stalk or a glass's slender upright.

clue.text: A scientist setting his sights on higher things

definitions.text: A scientist setting his sights on higher things

parts.words: A scientist setting his sights on higher things
parts.note: seems to be an ambitious researcher, but literally one who looks up at the heavens

explanation.definitionFit: An astronomer studies stars and planets through telescopes.

clue.text: Most hatcheries provide straw and reeds

indicators.note: the words provide the answer from within their letters

explanation.surface: Most poultry hatcheries supply straw and reeds for nesting.
explanation.definitionFit: Thatch is roofing material made of straw or reeds.

clue.text: Generally all at sea

explanation.surface: Usually completely confused.
explanation.definitionFit: On the whole, or literally out on the ocean, the main being the open sea.

clue.text: Information concerning a particular school

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Details about a specific school.
explanation.definitionFit: A genre is a style or category of art, as is a school of painting.

clue.text: Men met and worked out reparation

indicators.note: worked out suggests the letters are reorganised into a new order

explanation.surface: Some men gathered and negotiated compensation.
explanation.definitionFit: An amendment is a correction or making good, a form of redress.

clue.text: Play with no backing in London

parts.note: an act is a portion of a play, or to play a part

indicators.note: backing means the little word no is turned round to face backwards

explanation.surface: A theatre show without financial backers in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: ACTON is a district of west London; the definition just places it.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is a suburb located within the capital of England.

clue.text: The iron rule of the cat

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
a rule is a ruled line

explanation.surface: The household cat lays down the law with an iron hand.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes anything belonging to or like a cat or its family.

clue.text: Firm having clear lead on Mediterranean island

indicators.note: the lead of a word is its first letter, here taken from clear

parts.note: taken as written
Crete is the large Greek island in the Mediterranean

explanation.surface: A company has a clear lead in the market on a Greek island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clear lead on' looks like a phrase about a firm's market advantage; 'lead' only picks the first letter of 'clear'.
explanation.definitionFit: Concrete as an adjective means solid and definite, set hard.

clue.text: A nice party must be arranged, whatever the cost

indicators.note: arranged means the letters are put in a different order

explanation.surface: A nice party has to be organised, no matter the expense.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means regardless of price or sacrifice.

clue.text: The tale told about exemplary put-down

indicators.note: about means the story word is placed around the exemplary abbreviation

parts.note: a relation is a narrative, the telling of a tale
e.g. abbreviates exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: A story recounted about a model put-down.
explanation.definitionFit: Relegation is demotion, a sending down to a lower division or rank.

clue.text: The book-keeper

parts.note: seems to be an accountant, but literally one who keeps books in a collection

explanation.definitionFit: A librarian looks after a library's volumes.

clue.text: Some role!

explanation.surface: An actor exclaims about getting just a small role.
explanation.definitionFit: A portion of something, or an actor's character in a play.

clue.text: Let assets get dissipated to obtain flat

indicators.note: dissipated means scattered, so the letters are dispersed into a new order

explanation.surface: Letting your capital be squandered to buy an apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat' looks like a home to buy, but it means insipid.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasteless means dull or insipid, lacking flavour or sparkle.

clue.text: "It is, it is a -— thing to be a Pirate King" (Gilbert)

definitions.text: "It is, it is a -— thing to be a Pirate King" (Gilbert)

parts.words: "It is, it is a -— thing to be a Pirate King" (Gilbert)
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation from Gilbert and Sullivan's The Pirates of Penzance

explanation.walkthrough: The Pirates of Penzance is a comic opera by W S Gilbert and Arthur Sullivan; the Pirate King's song supplies the missing word.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means magnificent or splendid, as the pirate praises his trade.

clue.text: Commitment of French man of honour

parts.note: de is French for of
Bt abbreviates baronet, a hereditary title of honour

explanation.surface: The commitment shown by a decorated Frenchman.
explanation.definitionFit: Money owed is an obligation, something one is bound to pay.

clue.text: The juniors will get less fish

parts.note: under means less than, as in under ten

explanation.surface: The younger staff will be given a smaller portion of fish.

clue.text: Seafood obtained by double-dealing goody-goody

explanation.surface: Seafood got by a con played by a sanctimonious person.
explanation.definitionFit: Scampi are breaded langoustine tails, a British pub dish.

clue.text: Painting in water-colours

parts.note: seems to name a medium, watercolour, but means a picture whose subject is the colours of water, the sea

explanation.definitionFit: A seascape is a painting of a marine view.

clue.text: Self-controlled individual thus about to appear

indicators.note: about means the word for thus surrounds the little word to

parts.note: sic is Latin for thus

explanation.surface: A composed person is about to make an appearance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to appear' reads as 'soon to arrive'; here 'about' is the container signal and 'appear' merely links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoic endures hardship calmly without complaint.

clue.text: Fold note into envelope

indicators.note: into means the note goes inside the envelope

parts.note: a case is a covering or envelope

clue.text: This woman could cause a learner-driver to turn cold!

ice is cold, frozen water

explanation.surface: A woman who could make a nervous learner-driver go cold.
explanation.definitionFit: Alice is a woman's given name.

clue.text: A rotisserie ends up here

parts.note: a roast on a rotisserie ends up skewered on this rod, which is itself the turning part

explanation.definitionFit: A spit is a rotating rod for roasting meat over a fire.

clue.text: Dislike the sound of the old music-hall?

indicators.note: the sound of tells us the word is heard rather than written

parts.note: an odeum was an ancient building for musical performances

explanation.surface: Disliking the noise coming from a Victorian variety theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Odium is general hatred or disgust felt towards someone.

clue.text: Better to accept one's got to make do somehow

indicators.note: to accept means the word for better takes in the other piece

parts.note: to better something is to improve it

explanation.surface: Making things better means coping with whatever you have.
explanation.definitionFit: To extemporise is to manage with whatever is at hand, without preparation.

clue.text: Pleased to include well-liked moderate

in means fashionable or popular

clue.text: Storage accommodation for casts

explanation.surface: Garden huts used to store plaster casts.
explanation.definitionFit: Garden huts for storing tools, and a verb meaning throws off, as a snake its skin.
